transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-30
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ari Patel (Redwood CSM), Janelle Park (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (Harbor Head of ML), Ethan Price (Harbor PM), Samir Khan (Harbor IT Sec), Lina Gomez (Harbor DevOps)

[00:00] Ari Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining - this is Ari from Redwood, I'm the CSM on the account, and with me is Janelle our solutions engineer. Welcome, Maya, Ethan, Samir, Lina.
[00:08] Maya Rodriguez: Hi thanks, excited to get started.
[00:11] Ethan Price: Hey all.
[00:13] Janelle Park: Quick agenda - intro, security reqs, infra needs, pilot scope/timeline, and then action items. We'll leave time for Qs.
[00:20] Samir Khan: Sounds good. We mostly want to cover SSO, key management, and data residency up front.
[00:27] Ari Patel: Totally. Before we dive, can someone share a bit about the immediate use cases you're targeting for the pilot? Maya?
[00:33] Maya Rodriguez: Sure - our initial goal is twofold: 1) Move our patient triage assistant from a hosted open model to a more controlled deployment to lower latency and cost, and 2) run embeddings for search across patient-facing docs. We want to measure latency P95 and cost per 1k tokens; also want to validate privacy/compliance for PHI.
[00:52] Janelle Park: Good. For PHI we usually recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strong egress controls, depending on whether you need on-prem. Are you planning to keep data in-cloud or air-gapped?
[00:59] Lina Gomez: Cloud for now - but with strict VPC controls and KMS for encryption. We do not want anything landing in a shared host storage.
[01:08] Samir Khan: From security side, we need SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning ideally, audit logs retained 1 year, and CMKs for encryption. Also we need SOC2 and a security questionnaire answered.
[01:22] Ari Patel: We can cover that. Redwood Private supports customer KMS / HSM and audit log retention; Dedicated pools can be configured with customer-managed keys and VPC peering. We'll send SOC 2 and the security pack after the call.
[01:36] Ethan Price: Timeline - we want a 90-day pilot to validate perf and cost. Goal to be production-ready by end of Q1. Is that feasible?
[01:46] Janelle Park: Yes, 90 days is doable. We'll propose an initial smoke test week 1, benchmks week 2, and iterate on model/quantize config weeks 3-6.
[01:58] Maya Rodriguez: Benchmarks - we need sample payloads and throughput numbers. Also curious about KV cache behavior for the triage flows, since we use session context.
[02:09] Janelle Park: We have continuous batching and KV cache - sometimes exported in docs as "K V cache" and that confuses folks, but it's the same. For triage, prefix caching will help with repeated prompts and reduce token costs. We'll test that in the benchmark.
[02:25] Samir Khan: Compliance - do you support bringing our own CMKs in your hosted product? Concern is keys leaving our control.
[02:33] Ari Patel: For hosted Redwood we offer envelope encryption; for Dedicated/Private you can bring your own CMKs via KMS/HSM integrations. We'll send the KMS integration guide.
[02:44] Lina Gomez: For VPC peering, what egress rules are required? We run strict egress only to specific Redwood subnets.
[02:51] Janelle Park: We'll provide the subnet/CIDR ranges. Typical setup is VPC peering or PrivateLink; some customers use NAT with explicit egress. We'll include firewall rules doc.

[03:05] Ethan Price: Any limitations we should know about for the embeddings job? Memory? GPU?
[03:10] Janelle Park: Embeddings are CPU-friendly but if you're running large batch encoders we'll recommend dedicated CPU nodes. For vector search we'll also talk about approximate nearest neighbor options. We'll share recommended instance sizes.
[03:23] Maya Rodriguez: Also curious about model updates - can we pin versions during pilot to avoid drift?
[03:27] Ari Patel: Yes, you can pin model versions and we support rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallbacks if newer weights introduce regressions. That will be part of the rollback policy we propose.

[03:40] [small cross talk - coffee sounds]

[03:50] Samir Khan: On audit logs - how granular are they? Do they include token-level cost? We need to reconcile with our billing.
[03:58] Janelle Park: Audit logs include request metadata, user identity mapping (if SSO/SCIM is set), model id, timestamps, and token counts. Token-level cost breakdown is available in the console and via API.
[04:13] Maya Rodriguez: For the triage assistant we have long conversations - what about KV cache retention and query length limits? We often hit 8k tokens.
[04:20] Janelle Park: We support config for KV cache TTL and rolling windows; runtime picks kernels for long-context models. For >8k you might want to use a long-context variant; we can test with your payloads.

[04:36] Ethan Price: Ok let's run through a proposed schedule. Ari?
[04:40] Ari Patel: Week 0: onboarding docs and infra prep. Week 1: SSO + VPC peering config, initial smoke tests. Week 2: perf benchmarks with sample payloads. Weeks 3-6: tuning, quantization recommendations, cost optimizations. Weeks 7-12: production pilot and quality monitoring.
[04:58] Maya Rodriguez: That looks good. Can we have a checkpoint after benchmks to decide dedicated vs hosted?
[05:03] Janelle Park: Absolutely - we'll provide concrete latency/cost numbers and a recommended deployment based on throughput. Sometimes a hybrid routing policy works - hosted for low-sensitivity queries, Dedicated for PHI.

[05:18] Samir Khan: One more on legal/comms - the procurement team will want copies of the SOC2 and any CSA / ISO items. We'll follow up with a checklist.
[05:26] Ari Patel: I'll attach the security pack and our contact for the compliance questionnaire.

[05:35] Ethan Price: Support model - what SLA and escalation path do we get during pilot?
[05:40] Janelle Park: During pilot you'll have CSM (Ari) and a SE triage channel; Dedicated customers can opt into priority support with 1-hour P1 response. We'll outline the SLA options in the pricing doc.

[05:53] Maya Rodriguez: For the benchmarks, please include the quantization profile suggestions - we want to balance cost and latency; our triage needs sub-300ms P50 ideally.
[06:03] Janelle Park: We'll include quant profiles and typical perf numbers per GPU type. Note: GPU selection impacts kernel availability and long-context performance.

[06:18] Samir Khan: Anything else on network egress / data residency? We have a contract requirement that logs with PHI are kept in region.
[06:26] Ari Patel: We support region pinning for Dedicated / Private; we'll confirm region availability and retention policies.

[06:35] [pause - small typing noise]

[06:40] Ari Patel: Ok quick recap and next steps: Ari will send SSO, KMS, SOC2 pack; Janelle will schedule Dedicated demo and run an initial benchmarking checklist; Lina will share VPC/subnet details; Maya will confirm success metrics. We'll set weekly syncs starting 2026-10-07.
[06:58] Maya Rodriguez: That works, thanks.
[07:00] Ethan Price: Thanks all.
[07:02] Janelle Park: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hearings in product names (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of Dedicated), some filler words and short cross talk.
